title: UniFunc3D: Unified Active Spatial-Temporal Grounding for 3D Functionality Segmentation

problems.name: Spatio-Temporal and Object/Event-Level Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: UniFunc3D: Unified Active Spatial-Temporal Grounding for 3D Functionality Segmentation Functionality segmentation in 3D scenes requires an agent to ground implicit natural-language instructions into precise masks of fine-grained interactive elements.

problems.name: LLM Temporal Reasoning and Time Output Instability
problems.evidence_sentence: To address these limitations, we introduce UniFunc3D, a unified and training-free framework that consolidates semantic, temporal, and spatial reasoning within a single multimodal large language model (MLLM).

problems.name: Long-Video Evidence Sparsity and Efficient Selection
problems.evidence_sentence: We observe that these methods are limited by single-scale, passive and heuristic frame selection.

methods.name: Object/Event/Spatio-Temporal Modules
methods.evidence_sentence: These approaches often begin with a “visually blind” reasoning stage where a text-only LLM (i.e., LLaMA-3.1-9B) to decompose the input text description into two kinds of object: the contextual object (i.e., the object that contains or is related to the functional object) and the functional object (i.e., the ultimate object(s) or parts to segment).

methods.name: LLM Reasoning, Agentic Workflows, or RL Post-Training
methods.evidence_sentence: By consolidating semantic, temporal, and spatial reasoning into a single forward pass, UniFunc3D performs joint reasoning to ground task decomposition in direct visual evidence.

methods.name: Query-Conditioned Frame/Clip Selection
methods.evidence_sentence: We observe that these methods are limited by single-scale, passive and heuristic frame selection.

methods.name: Coarse-to-Fine or Hierarchical Localization
methods.evidence_sentence: Our approach introduces active spatial-temporal grounding with a coarse-to-fine strategy.
